stories.title: CFTC opens door to Bitcoin reserves at US exchanges, with a 20% catch
stories.summary: The CFTC has proposed a path for US-regulated exchanges to hold Bitcoin as a reserve asset, according to CryptoSlate. The proposal reportedly includes a condition tied to a 20% threshold. Available reporting does not spell out the exact mechanics of that condition.
stories.whyItMatters: Reserve rules for regulated exchanges shape how much institutional money can treat Bitcoin as a held asset, not just a traded one.
whatToWatch: Final CFTC rule text and its 20% condition
Which exchanges respond or apply first
questions: What does the 20% threshold actually limit?
Does this apply to all CFTC-regulated exchanges or only some?

sources.title: The CFTC opens the door to Bitcoin reserves at US exchanges with a 20% catch

stories.title: Researchers say they found a way to make Bitcoin bridge testing much cheaper
stories.summary: Researchers report a method to test Bitcoin bridges at much lower cost, per CryptoSlate. Bridges connect Bitcoin to other blockchains and have been a frequent target of major hacks. Cheaper testing could let developers find flaws before funds move through a bridge.
stories.whyItMatters: Bridge exploits have drained large sums from crypto users, so lower-cost testing tools could cut future incident risk.
whatToWatch: Whether bridge projects adopt the new testing method
Any audits or vulnerability reports that result
questions: Which bridge protocols plan to use this method?
How does it compare with existing audit practices?

sources.title: Researchers find a way to make Bitcoin bridges dramatically cheaper to test

stories.title: Banks seek Fed funding access on holidays as Wall Street weighs longer settlement hours
stories.summary: US banks want access to Federal Reserve funding on holidays, CryptoSlate reports, as Wall Street moves toward longer settlement windows. Crypto markets already trade around the clock, so this shift would narrow a gap with traditional finance. The report does not name which banks are asking.
stories.whyItMatters: Longer settlement hours and holiday Fed access would change how liquidity moves between traditional finance and always-on crypto markets.
whatToWatch: The Fed's response to the request
Any timeline set for longer settlement hours
questions: Which banks are driving this request?
Would the Fed grant holiday access, and under what terms?

sources.title: US banks want access to Fed funding on holidays as Wall Street prepares for longer settlement hours

stories.title: Ansem claims a wallet hack after 87 million ANSEM tokens were dumped, but on-chain data raises doubts
stories.summary: Crypto influencer Ansem says a wallet hack caused an 87 million token dump of ANSEM, according to CryptoSlate. On-chain data is reportedly raising questions about that explanation. The report does not detail what the data shows.
stories.whyItMatters: Large token dumps by influencers often crash prices for followers who bought in, so the real cause matters to anyone holding the token.
whatToWatch: Results of any on-chain investigation into the transaction
Whether Ansem provides further evidence of a hack
questions: Was this a hack or an insider sale?
How has the ANSEM community and price reacted?

sources.title: Ansem claims wallet hack after an 87 million ANSEM token dump, but on-chain data raises questions

stories.title: XRP's shrinking exchange supply may not mean what investors think
stories.summary: XRP balances on exchanges have been falling, a trend some read as bullish because it suggests coins moving into long-term holding. CryptoSlate reports that reading may be misleading, though the available summary does not detail the alternative explanation.
stories.whyItMatters: Exchange-supply figures are a widely used bullish signal, so a misread could skew sentiment-driven XRP trading.
whatToWatch: Further analysis on where the XRP supply is actually going
questions: What is actually driving the decline in exchange balances?
Is it genuine holding, exchange consolidation, or something else?

sources.title: XRP’s shrinking exchange supply may be telling investors the wrong story

stories.title: Hong Kong wants banks to get approval before holding customer crypto
stories.summary: Hong Kong regulators want banks to secure approval before they hold customers' cryptocurrency, CryptoSlate reports. This would add a formal regulatory step for banks that want to offer crypto custody. No further detail on the approval criteria was in the available report.
stories.whyItMatters: Hong Kong has been positioning itself as a crypto hub, so clearer custody rules affect how banks there can serve crypto clients.
whatToWatch: Publication of the formal rule and its timeline
questions: What criteria will regulators use to grant approval?
How long will the approval process take?

sources.title: Hong Kong wants banks to secure new approval before holding customers’ crypto

stories.title: Eric Trump-linked Bitcoin miner jumps 17% on $150 million deal to avoid selling BTC
stories.summary: A Bitcoin mining company linked to Eric Trump rose 17% after a $150 million deal that lets it avoid selling its Bitcoin, according to CryptoSlate. Miners often sell BTC to cover running costs, so this financing lets the company keep more coins on its balance sheet.
stories.whyItMatters: It shows a miner using financing instead of selling Bitcoin to manage costs, a sign of how miners are coping with price pressure.
whatToWatch: How the $150 million financing is structured and used
The miner's Bitcoin holdings over coming months
questions: Is the deal debt, equity, or another structure?

sources.title: Eric Trump’s Bitcoin miner surges 17% after $150 million deal to avoid selling BTC

stories.title: Bitcoin faces new tariff threat as its drop toward $60,000 squeezes miners harder than 2022
stories.summary: Bitcoin faces a familiar macro threat as the US prepares another round of tariffs, CryptoSlate reports. Separately, the outlet reports that Bitcoin's slide toward $60,000 is testing miners harder than the 2022 crypto winter did. Together, the two reports point to a tougher stretch for both the market and the mining industry.
stories.whyItMatters: Tariff-driven macro stress and miner strain both affect Bitcoin's price stability and the health of its mining industry.
whatToWatch: Details and timing of the new tariffs
Signs of miner capitulation or consolidation
questions: How severe would the new tariffs be?
Which miners are most at risk if the price stays near $60,000?

sources.title: Bitcoin faces a familiar macro threat as the US prepares another round of tariffs
Bitcoin’s $60,000 bear market is testing miners harder than the 2022 crypto winter

stories.title: Prediction market bets placed just before big news could soon be easier to trace
stories.summary: It may soon be easier to trace prediction market bets placed right before major news breaks, CryptoSlate reports. The development touches concerns about traders profiting from advance knowledge on prediction market platforms. The report does not name the specific tool or method involved.
stories.whyItMatters: Insider-style betting ahead of news undermines trust in prediction markets, a sector gaining financial and political weight.
whatToWatch: Which platforms or tools adopt the new tracing method
Any investigations that follow from it
questions: Who is building this tracing capability?
Would it apply to past bets or only future ones?

sources.title: Prediction market bets placed just before big news could soon be easier to trace
